statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of the credential-free public route. The supplied URL redirects to the localized Microsoft Forms product landing; authenticated form creation and account surfaces were explicitly outside this run.

paths.description: Credential-free public Microsoft Forms product landing reached by the supplied redirect. Represents the only public content template and the discover/compare/start journey. Conditions: desktop, mobile, dark preference, reduced motion, contrast preference, keyboard focus, no-JS crawler, cold load, and repeated scrolling. Not covered: authenticated Forms editor/response flows, checkout, or account management because they are separate credentialed products.

findings.summary: The page does not adapt its light surfaces to the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to the light capture: white page, white navigation, and light hero remain unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare `color-scheme: light dark` and use `prefers-color-scheme` or `light-dark()` for surfaces, text, controls, and browser chrome.

findings.summary: The rendered page disappears under `prefers-contrast: more`.
findings.evidence: The high-contrast screenshot is entirely blank although the paired probe confirms 3,314+ characters remain in the DOM and `matchMedia("(prefers-contrast: more)")` is true.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit contrast-mode CSS for rules that suppress or paint content transparently; retain visible text, controls, focus indicators, and imagery under contrast preferences and forced colours.

findings.summary: The optional-cookie banner dominates the initial mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: At 360×800 the consent block consumes roughly the first 345 px before product navigation and content, delaying the “Microsoft Forms” purpose and primary actions.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-preserving consent surface; keep Reject as prominent as Accept and move detail behind an expandable disclosure without hiding the primary page.

findings.summary: The page adapts at the viewport level but exposes no container-query implementation.
findings.evidence: The CSS feature probe found responsive and modern interaction rules but no `@container` token; this component-heavy landing page is therefore coupled to global viewport breakpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards, CTA groups, and media panels containment and size-aware `@container` rules, retaining viewport fallbacks where needed.

findings.summary: Many visible footer links have undersized hit areas.
findings.evidence: The target probe found dozens of visible links only 16 px high; these are below comfortable touch-target guidance even though keyboard outlines are generally present.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase link line boxes and spacing so interactive targets reach at least 24×24 CSS px, preferably 44×44 for primary mobile controls, without relying on text glyph bounds alone.

findings.summary: Cold-load Core Web Vitals are far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 17.2 s and CLS 0.589 with performance score 27; the independent trace still measured LCP 3.46 s and 534 ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the hero LCP resource, reserve space for late content, reduce render-blocking CSS/JS, and split/defer non-critical work; verify on representative mobile throttling.

findings.summary: The page shifts substantially during the Lighthouse load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.589, while the image audit found 36 of 41 images without explicit width/height attributes, a concrete source of unreserved layout space.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or `aspect-ratio` for every image and reserve stable slots for consent, navigation, fonts, and deferred modules.

findings.summary: Long main-thread tasks block responsiveness during load.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded three long tasks, the longest 432.52 ms, with 534.24 ms total blocking time; Lighthouse reported 310 ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Break synchronous work into scheduled chunks, remove synchronous XHR, and defer analytics and non-visible components until idle or interaction.

findings.summary: The landing page delivers a large, fragmented critical load.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 119 requests and 4,406,313 transferred bytes, including 64 scripts (2.43 MB) and seven fonts (1.15 MB).
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce font variants, consolidate or defer scripts, confirm render-blocking candidates against DOM placement, and set useful caching for immutable assets.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped JavaScript and CSS are unused on first load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 443 KiB unused JavaScript and 346 KiB unused CSS; one global stylesheet is 98% unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split and component-split bundles, purge unused global CSS, and conditionally load navigation, chat, analytics, and product modules only when needed.

findings.summary: Image markup omits dimensions and responsive source selection.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 36/41 images without dimensions, nine without responsive sources, two oversized assets, and one legacy-format asset.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions, `srcset`/`sizes`, and appropriately encoded responsive variants from the image CDN; preserve meaningful alt text.

findings.summary: Deprecated unload handlers and synchronous XHR remain in production bundles.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three deprecation warnings: two unload listeners and a synchronous main-thread XMLHttpRequest.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload telemetry with `visibilitychange`/`pagehide` and `sendBeacon`, and replace synchronous XHR with asynchronous fetch.

findings.summary: The advertised sitemap endpoint does not return a sitemap.
findings.evidence: Fetching `/sitemap.xml` returned status 200 but an HTML Microsoft content page rather than XML, weakening route discovery and robots/sitemap consistency.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid XML sitemap at the declared location (or advertise the real sitemap in robots.txt) and include the canonical localized Forms landing URL.

findings.summary: The product landing has social tags but no structured entity data.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found Open Graph title/description/url but zero JSON-LD blocks for the Microsoft Forms software/product entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org `SoftwareApplication` or `Product` JSON-LD that matches the visible offer and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie posture are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, CSP, and Trusted Types are present, but CSP permits `unsafe-eval`/`unsafe-inline`; nosniff is absent. All three observed cookies use SameSite=None and MUID lasts 390 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove `unsafe-eval`, adopt nonce/hash-only script policy, add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and narrow SameSite and lifetime where cross-site use is not required.

findings.summary: The first load contacts a broad third-party and telemetry surface.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe observed 14 third-party origins, including Microsoft event endpoints, RUM, and Vidyard; the HAR transferred 4.4 MB before any audited consent action.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory each origin, defer optional analytics/media until consent or interaction, batch telemetry, and remove vendors that do not support the page’s primary task.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The header probe found no Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, or explicit X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors directive.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a restrictive Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, add nosniff, and prevent unwanted framing with CSP `frame-ancestors` (or X-Frame-Options as legacy defence).

findings.summary: Almost all meaningful product content depends on JavaScript.
findings.evidence: The discoverability primitive found only 4% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML, classified the response as a JS shell, and showed the crawler view without the product page.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the heading, descriptive copy, primary links, navigation, and core sections; layer interactive carousels and enhancements after usable HTML.

findings.summary: A script failure leaves the core public page effectively blank.
findings.evidence: The no-JavaScript crawler capture contains only a tiny shell and 4% of rendered content, so a blocked or failed script removes the page’s purpose and recovery path.
findings.suggestedFix: Ship resilient HTML for core content and provide an actionable failure message/retry path when enhancement bundles cannot load.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not consistently resolution- or format-efficient.
findings.evidence: The image audit found no modern-format images, nine missing responsive sources, two oversized images, and 36 missing intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the image CDN to negotiate AVIF/WebP, emit `srcset`/`sizes`, and constrain each request to its rendered slot and device density.

findings.summary: The page performs disproportionate script and telemetry work for a marketing landing page.
findings.evidence: The HAR contains 64 scripts and the trace records 534 ms blocking time; Lighthouse identifies 443 KiB unused JS and deprecated synchronous XHR.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally import non-critical modules, defer analytics/background processing, and remove synchronous or duplicate work.

findings.summary: Third-party, font, and script bytes dominate the page budget.
findings.evidence: The 4.4 MB load includes 2.43 MB of scripts, 1.15 MB of fonts, and 14 third-party origins for a text-and-image product landing.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route-level byte/request budget, reduce font variants and third parties, and lazy-load nonessential media and integrations after intent.

findings.summary: Many visible links do not provide a sufficiently large interaction target.
findings.evidence: The target probe found dozens of visible footer and utility links with only 16 px-high boxes; mobile reflow itself had no horizontal overflow and the viewport permits scaling.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase the line box, padding, or spacing around compact links to provide at least a 24×24 CSS px target, while preserving the successful mobile reflow.

taskList.title: Fix the critical load path and visual stability
Server-render the public Forms landing and failure fallback
Harden contrast and dark preference rendering
Reduce scripts, fonts, telemetry, and third parties
Complete browser security policy headers and cookie restrictions
Make image delivery responsive, stable, and modern
Reduce the mobile consent footprint and enlarge small targets
Remove deprecated unload and synchronous XHR code
Add product structured data and a valid sitemap
Decouple reusable components with container queries
Increase compact utility and footer link hit areas
